documents.title: Admissions Deadlines
documents.content: Riverside Community College accepts applications for the fall semester through March 1st and for the spring semester through October 15th. Early decision applicants must submit all materials by December 1st for the following fall. Application fee waivers are available for students with demonstrated financial need. Decisions are released within six weeks of the applicable deadline.

documents.title: Financial Aid Overview
documents.content: Riverside Community College financial aid packages combine need-based grants, merit scholarships, and federal work-study. Students must file the FAFSA by February 1st to be considered for the full range of institutional aid. Award letters are sent within four weeks of a completed FAFSA. Appeals for special circumstances are reviewed by the financial aid committee on a rolling basis.

documents.title: Course Registration Guide
documents.content: Continuing students register for courses through the student portal during their assigned registration window, which opens based on completed credit hours. New students register during new-student orientation with an academic advisor. Waitlisted courses are processed automatically as seats open, and students are notified by email. A late registration fee applies after the first week of the term.

documents.title: Campus Policies and Code of Conduct
documents.content: Riverside Community College expects all students to act with academic integrity and personal respect toward the community. Prohibited conduct includes plagiarism, harassment, and unauthorized use of college systems. Reports of misconduct are reviewed by the Office of Student Conduct, and students may appeal a finding within ten business days of the decision letter.

documents.title: Contact and Support Directory
documents.content: The Admissions Office is reachable at admissions@riverside.example.edu or by phone during business hours, Monday through Friday. The Financial Aid Office handles award questions and appeals. The IT Help Desk supports student portal access issues. General campus safety concerns should be directed to Campus Security's non-emergency line.

documents.title: Housing and Meal Plans
documents.content: On-campus housing applications open alongside admission offers and are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis once a deposit is paid. All first-year residential students are required to select a meal plan; commuter students may opt into a reduced meal plan. Housing contracts run for a full academic year and cannot be cancelled after the fall census date except for documented emergencies.

documents.title: Transfer Credit Policy
documents.content: Riverside Community College accepts transfer credit from regionally accredited institutions for courses completed with a grade of C or higher. Transfer credit evaluations are completed by the Registrar within three weeks of receiving an official transcript. A maximum of 60 semester credits may transfer toward a bachelor's degree. Course equivalency appeals are reviewed by the relevant academic department.
